explain.say: The bottom layer of the skin grows faster than the layers around it, so it buckles into folds, like a rug pushed against a wall. These folds become the ridges of your fingerprint.

faq.a: Before birth, the deepest layer of the skin grows faster than the layers around it and buckles into folds. These folds become the ridges that make up your fingerprint.
asks: What makes the lines on fingers?

faq.a: Genes affect the general type of pattern, but the exact details depend on tiny chance differences in the womb, like finger pad shape, growth speed and pressure, so no two prints are the same.
asks: Why are fingerprints different for everyone?

faq.q: When is a fingerprint pattern finished?
faq.a: Ridges begin to form at about 10 weeks after fertilisation and the pattern is complete by about 17 weeks. After that it never changes.

faq.q: Do fingerprints change as you grow?
faq.a: They get larger as your hands grow, but the pattern of ridges stays exactly the same throughout life. Even after small cuts heal, the ridges usually grow back in the same pattern.
asks: Are fingerprints the same when you are old?

faq.q: What are loops, whorls and arches?
faq.a: They are the three main fingerprint patterns. Loops curve back on themselves and are the most common; whorls form circles or spirals; arches rise in a wave across the finger and are the rarest.
asks: What are the types of fingerprints?
What is the most common fingerprint pattern?

facts: Fingerprint ridges start forming at around 10 weeks after fertilisation and are set by about 17 weeks.
Loops are the most common fingerprint pattern, found on roughly 60 to 65 percent of fingers.
